framework_rationale: The submission imports only tensorcircuit alongside standard numerical/optimization libraries (jax, numpy, optax) and performs all core quantum operations using tensorcircuit with the JAX backend: building single-qubit RX-RZ-RY block unitaries via tc.Circuit(1), constructing and simulating the 22-qubit ansatz via tc.Circuit(n_qubits) with c.x, c.any, native c.cmz(*selected_qubits) for the 18-qubit controlled-Z hyperedge, and c.state(), and evaluating the TFIM Hamiltonian matrix-vector product via tc.quantum.PauliStringSum2MVP. No other quantum framework is imported or used, and there is no raw NumPy/JAX simulator bypass.
cheating_rationale: No signs of hardcoding, hidden answer access, test/reward tampering, or evaluator exploitation. All circuit, Hamiltonian, initialization, and optimization hyperparameters are read dynamically from config, and the VQE optimization legitimately computes energies and gradients from the parameterized quantum state.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches all specifications in Problem 10: initializes the Neel computational-basis state using initial_ones, applies n_layers of per-qubit RX-RZ-RY rotation blocks (faithfully fused per qubit via tc.Circuit(1).matrix() and applied with c.any) followed by the fixed 18-qubit controlled-Z gate on selected_qubits via c.cmz, constructs the exact open-boundary TFIM Hamiltonian via matrix-vector product (PauliStringSum2MVP with -zz_strength Z_i Z_{i+1} and -x_strength X_i), initializes parameters from N(0, initial_parameter_scale^2) with the configured seed, optimizes with optax.adam at learning_rate for max_steps updates, records energy density <H>/n_qubits immediately before each update, uses an exact Hermitian stop-gradient trick (2*eh - stop_gradient(eh) with stop_gradient(H|psi>)) that preserves both the exact value and exact gradient, prints nothing, and returns NumPy arrays with the exact required keys and shapes.
implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation errors were found. The Hermitian expectation gradient optimization (stop_gradient on H|psi> combined with 2*eh - stop_gradient(eh)) is mathematically exact for real parameters and Hermitian H, dtype complex128/float64 precision is enabled, and edge cases like max_steps <= 0 or small selected_qubits counts are handled cleanly.
